name: Riantana
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.quote: Als we het nodig achten aan te geven welke lettergreep betoond wordt, dan doen we dat door een accent grave op de klinker van die syllabe te schrijven; tot welke soort de betoning in deze taal behoort, zullen we hier niet uitmaken.
new_statements.translation: If we find it necessary to indicate which syllable is stressed, we do so by writing a grave accent on the vowel of that syllable; to what kind the accentuation in this language belongs, we shall not decide here.
new_statements.citation: Drabbe, Peter. 1949. Bijzonderheden uit de talen van Frederik-Hendrik-eiland: Kimaghama, Ndom en Riantana. Bijdragen tot de Taal-, Land- en Volkenkunde 105(1): 1-24. doi:10.1163/22134379-90002486
new_statements.locator: Introduction, numbered orthography remark 8 (between remark 6 'Voor Riantana...' and remark 9 'In Kimàghama...'), c. pp. 3-4 (Usher cites the inventories at Drabbe 1949: 3-4; snippets carry no page number)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Quote check: the passage is present verbatim in the held snippet digest; raw in gbf_q33.xml, gbf_q29/30.xml). I then obtained the FULL open-access article, which the first reader could not: Wayback CDX lists captures of Brill's OA PDF (20200213153911, 20231116225003) and the 2020 capture downloaded cleanly (25 pp., iText text layer): +, addendum appended (stamp from date -u). In the real article the quote sits on printed p. 4, numbered remark 8, word for word: 'Als we het nodig achten aan te geven welke lettergreep betoond wordt, dan doen we dat door een accent grave op de klinker van die syllabe te schrijven; tot welke soort de betoning in deze taal behoort, zullen we hier niet uitmaken.'…
new_statements.rule_in_words: No positional rule is given. Drabbe marks the stressed syllable ad hoc with a grave accent on individual forms and explicitly declines to characterise the accent (stress vs. pitch). His Riantana wordlist forms (as re-transcribed by Usher) carry the mark on varying syllables: roughly half final (tʲaˈra 'break', aˈga 'sweet potato', moˈra), a quarter initial (ˈmɛtʏ 'stone', ˈtraβʏ, ˈpiβo), some medial (kaˈraβo, βeˈrimo) - i.e. position not predictable from this source.
new_statements.exceptions: None; the remark follows the Ndom orthography note (remark 7) and says 'in deze taal' (singular), so it is not fully certain from the snippet whether the disclaimer about the nature of the accent is meant for Ndom alone or for all three island languages; the grave-marking convention itself is applied to Riantana and Kimaghama forms throughout the article.
new_statements.domain_note: Isolated citation forms in a comparative wordlist (pp. 14-24); no discussion of word vs phrase domain.
new_statements.identity_note: All sources describe the same variety: Riantana/Riandana of the six northern villages of Kimaam (Frederik-Hendrik/Kolopom) Island (Drabbe 1949; Choi 2015 probably the same dialect per Usher) = Glottolog rian1263. Drabbe's accent remark 8 sits in a joint orthography introduction for Kimaghama (kima1246), Riantana and Ndom (ndom1245) and immediately follows the Ndom note, so its scope over Riantana specifically is inferred, not explicit, from the snippet.

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy. n.d. 'Riandana' (also 'Kolopom', 'Kimaghama', 'Ndom'). Newguineaworld, DokuWiki hosted at Univ. Zurich.
sources.note: Second-hand phonology digest of Drabbe 1949 and Choi 2015 (cites Choi 2015: 16-26 phonology, 24-25 final-vowel devoicing). States no stress rule; re-transcribes Drabbe's Riantana forms with his accent marks (of 102 distinct stress-marked forms in the tables: 53 final, 24 initial, 14 medial, 13 on monosyllabic parts); twice notes 'Drabbe hears the second vowel as stressed' in CwV/CjV sequences.
